newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - July 3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - July 3.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Living up to expectations, the holiday-shortened week offered little but lackluster trading, Random Lengths said in its end-week market review. Many framing lumber prices drifted down but the drops were partly offset by gains in Southern Pine, the lumber reporting agency said.
Outside of the Southern Pine market, buyers were generally able to find quick shipments of whatever they wanted, allowing them to limit purchases to immediate needs, Random Lengths said.
Wholesalers helped to keep dealers supplied with prompt wood by pushing to get rid of what they owned prior to the long weekend break in the U.S. for Independence Day.
A few producers sought to pad their order files by pursuing "price-at-time-of-shipment" deals with selected customers, th4e agency said.
While acknowledging that a substantial volume of wood is moving through the pipeline, buyers also noted that the latest data showed strong production in all regions.
Sellers were encouraged by a report that sales of new homes rebounded in May, as well as the Federal Reserve's decision to hold the line on interest rates, Random Lengths said.

Labor negotiations in western Canada provided little new grist for the rumor mill. Negotiations continued between woodworkers and employers in British Columbia, while pulp and paper talks were scheduled to resume July 4.
